$comment: Pins the SDK so every machine in the fleet builds with the SAME toolchain.
Why this file exists (added 2026-08-22): box1 had only 10.0.301 while two newly
added fleet machines had 10.0.400, and with no global.json `dotnet` silently picks
the newest SDK installed on each host. Three machines would have built the project
three different ways and nothing would have reported it.
Why 10.0.301 and not the newer 10.0.400: ADR-002/003 pin it, and ADR-001's central
finding -- that the ASP.NET Core Web SDK accepts a hand-authored .vbproj and emits
zero C# -- was measured on 10.0.301. That result is the project's dominant retired
risk. Moving the SDK would put it back on the table for no benefit.
rollForward disable is deliberate: an exact-match requirement is the only setting
that makes the ADR pin actually true. A machine without 10.0.301 now fails loudly
at restore with a clear message, instead of building something subtly different.
